title: Replay candidate reading rules over 50 past requests via subcommand
summary: Add an `athena` subcommand that applies the reading acceptance rules to a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason. After checks pass, run it from the base and candidate builds over the last 50 recorded requests with accepted readings. The replay result is the list the candidate refuses that the base accepted. It is recorded, shown to the verifier, and a candidate is held if more than 10% of those 50 are newly refused, unless its criteria intend a higher rate. The goal is to stop a refusal rule from landing untried, and the audience is the maintainers and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Fixture-based tests; cargo test and clippy -D warnings pass.
Criteria run tests that exercise the replay and hold.
The check is that a rule change is listed as newly refused on fixture history.
The hold is enforced in the run pipeline, not by prose.
An empty history is reported as no replay, not as a pass.
Docs and the changelog are written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Per the user's reply there is no flag detecting refusal-rule changes; every candidate is replayed.
The new subcommand lives in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs and calls the acceptance rules in reading.rs.
Records are read through existing record-reading code; tests use fixture records.
The 10% threshold is a code constant; it applies to newly refused requests out of the replayed requests.
With an empty newly-refused list no model call is made, and an empty history is reported as no replay, not a pass.
'Criteria intend a higher rate' is detected by a code check on the candidate's acceptance criteria text.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new athena subcommand takes a stored request and reading and prints accept or refuse with the reason, using the same acceptance rules as reading.rs; a test runs it on fixtures (cargo test).
A test builds a candidate-like rule change over fixture records and shows the newly refused requests (refused by candidate, accepted by base) are listed (cargo test -p athena-core).
A test shows the replay uses only the latest 50 requests that have accepted readings, and that an empty history is reported as no replay, not a pass (cargo test).

A test shows a candidate newly refusing more than 10% is held with the list, a candidate at or under 10% is not held, and a candidate whose criteria intend a higher rate is not held, with the replay still recorded (cargo test).
A test shows that with no rule change the replay list is empty and makes no model call (cargo test).

crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs runs the replay after checks pass for every candidate, using the base and candidate builds, and records the result; a test covers the hold path in the pipeline (cargo test).

A test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs shows the verifier brief carries the replay summary (newly refused count, total, list) and stays within its size limit with a long list (cargo test -p athena-context).
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the subcommand, the replay, the 10% hold and the verifier brief summary.
No governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) changes; the 10% threshold is a code constant.

out_of_scope: Detecting refusal-rule changes by a flag or by matching diffs
departures: Larger than the reference: new CLI subcommand, a base and candidate build replay in the run pipeline, and a brief change.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted time from refusal rules that stop drains and refuse their own fixes.
hard_reason: Adds a gate that can hold candidates and changes the run pipeline, the verifier brief and how readings are judged.
